newsitem.title: USA: Hallwood to self-tender shares, some debt.
newsitem.headline: Hallwood to self-tender shares, some debt.

text.p: The Hallwood Group Inc said Friday that it will self-tender up to 300,000 shares representing 19.1 percent of its outstanding shares and also its 13.5 percent subordinated debentures due July 31, 2009.
The company said it will buy its common shares $27.50 a share cash. It said its shares closed at $24.50 on the New York Stock Exchange April 30, 1997.
The company said it will prorate its purchases if more than 300,000 shares of its stock are tendered.

The company said it will buy its 1991 and its 1992 series bonds for $80 per $100 in principal amount and all its 1996 series for $70 per $100. It said it would buy as much of its 1989 series as possible at $95 per $100 from the funds left after buying the other series.
It said it will not make payment for accrued interest on any of the bonds tendered.
Hallwood said the offers begin on or about May 8 and expire June 16, unless extended. It said it will fund the offers from cash on hand.
